title: Improving search efficiency via adaptive acquisition function selection in discrete black-box optimization
summary: In discrete-variable black-box optimization, the number of candidate solutions grows combinatorially, while each evaluation is often expensive. Therefore, it is important to identify promising solutions efficiently within a limited number of trials. Bayesian Optimization of Combinatorial Structures (BOCS), an existing parametric method, works effectively when only a small amount of data is available.
